title: Brihadisvara: A Tower of Granite

segments.say: In the year ten-ten, in Thanjavur, a Chola king finished the tallest temple tower India had ever seen. And there's no granite quarry nearby.
The king was Rajaraja Chola the First. His temple, dedicated to Shiva, is called Brihadisvara, the Big Temple.

anim.title: The tower
items: Capstone said to weigh about 80 tonnes

segments.say: Its tower rises about sixty-six metres, all in granite. The stone at the very top is said to weigh about eighty tonnes. How it got up there is still debated.
It's a Dravida temple, with a stepped, pyramid tower called a vimana. Here the vimana dwarfs the gateways. In later southern temples, it was the gateways that grew huge.
Its walls carry inscriptions listing gifts, staff and even the temple's dancers and musicians. A temple was also a bank, a school and an employer.
With two later Chola temples, it's a UNESCO World Heritage Site: the Great Living Chola Temples, still in worship today.
For GS One: Rajaraja the First, ten-ten, Dravida style, and a granite vimana that towers over everything.

sources: UNESCO World Heritage List, 'Great Living Chola Temples' (Brihadisvara, Thanjavur, inscribed 1987; extended 2004 with Gangaikondacholapuram and Airavatesvara, Darasuram); Brihadisvara built by Rajaraja I, completed 1010; vimana about 66 m
